obligation: G017 - identify and fix the dominant stage
discriminator: Batch size holds the DISPATCH COUNT constant while multiplying the arithmetic per dispatch. Flat wall means launch-bound; linear wall means compute-bound.
ANSWER: A batch-1 decode step is ~85% (q3) to ~93% (bf16) FIXED COST that does not scale with the work done. That is why quantized decode achieves only 18-23% of peak bandwidth: the GPU is mostly idle across many small dispatches, so removing bytes cannot help. It also explains why bf16 -- with 3.5x the bytes per token -- shows a HIGHER fixed fraction: its dispatches are the same count and its marginal work is larger, so both arms are launch-dominated at B=1.
THE_FIX_IS_MEASURED_NOT_PROPOSED: Batching amortises the fixed cost directly. q3-g128 goes from 8.788 ms/token at B=1 to 1.800 at B=16, a 4.9x per-token speedup; bf16 goes 13.387 -> 1.695, 7.9x. No representation change, no kernel written.
WHERE_IT_APPLIES_TO_THIS_HARNESS: Single-stream chat decode cannot batch tokens. But the SCIENTIST does not run one stream: every capability evaluation in this campaign runs 8 independent prompts SEQUENTIALLY. Those are exactly independent streams and batch perfectly. At B=8 the measured per-token cost is 2.298 ms against 8.788, so the evaluator's generation phase is carrying a ~3.8x avoidable cost on every arm measured today.
RELATION_TO_THE_ABLATION: Consistent. Attention owning 40.8% and router+gather+combine 28.2% at B=1 are shares of a step that is ~85% launch overhead -- those stages have the most dispatches, not the most arithmetic. Expert matmuls own the arithmetic and only 17.4% of the wall.
CAVEAT: Batching raises resident bytes (KV cache per stream) and latency per request; it is a throughput fix, correct for an evaluation harness and wrong for interactive single-stream use.
